stories.title: Serena and Venus Williams Accept Cincinnati Doubles Wild Card — First Match Together Since 2022 US Open

x_posts.label: Post 1-1
x_posts.text:
Serena and Venus Williams are back.

They've accepted a Cincinnati doubles wild card — their first match together since the 2022 US Open.

Serena's comeback continues. The sisters are on the same side of the net again.

#Tennis #CincinnatiOpen #WilliamsSisters

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text:
Last time Serena and Venus Williams played doubles together: 2022 US Open.

Tonight they're back on court in Cincinnati with a wild card.

It doesn't matter what happens. This is already something.

#CincinnatiOpen #Tennis #Serena

facebook.long_form:
They're back.

Serena Williams and Venus Williams have accepted a wild card into the 2026 Cincinnati Open women's doubles draw — their first match together since the 2022 US Open. Serena, now 44, is continuing her comeback after she had to pull out of their Wimbledon 2026 doubles partnership due to a right knee issue. Cincinnati is her statement: the comeback is still on.

Venus received a singles wild card as well. Her singles year has been a difficult one — 0-14 in 2026 heading into the tournament — but the doubles call-up carries a different kind of meaning.

The Williams sisters built their doubles legacy into something historic. Fourteen Grand Slam doubles titles together. The most iconic siblings in tennis. The last time they played together was the 2022 US Open, and the sport has missed this.

Tonight in Cincinnati, they share a court again. Win or lose, this is one of those moments that makes you love tennis.

What's your favourite Williams sisters doubles memory?

---

stories.title: Swiatek Crushes Arango 6-3, 6-0 — Toronto Champion Arrives in Cincinnati With Force

x_posts.label: Post 2-1
x_posts.text:
Iga Swiatek. 6-3, 6-0. 72 minutes. Seven straight wins.

She won Toronto last week. She just crushed the player who beat Venus Williams.

The defending Cincinnati champion is here and she means business.

#CincinnatiOpen #Tennis #Swiatek

x_posts.label: Post 2-2
x_posts.text:
Swiatek won 5 of 7 return games and 7 of 8 service games vs. Arango.

6-3, 6-0. 72 minutes. Now she faces Sakkari in R3 — H2H 5-4 Swiatek.

She's locked in.

#Tennis #CincinnatiOpen #WTA

facebook.long_form:
This is what in-form Iga Swiatek looks like.

On Sunday in Cincinnati, the defending champion opened her title defence by beating Emiliana Arango — the same Colombian who had just eliminated Venus Williams — 6-3, 6-0 in 72 minutes. Seven straight match wins. Five of seven return games won. Seven of eight service games held.

Swiatek won Toronto last week, beating Rybakina 6-2, 6-3 in the final to snap a 10-month title drought. But Sunday was a different kind of statement. She didn't just win; she made it look routine.

The four-time Roland Garros champion and two-time US Open champion now faces Maria Sakkari (GRE) in R3, leading the H2H 5-4. Sakkari is a dangerous player on any given day. It's exactly the kind of test that separates players in form from players who just got a good draw.

Swiatek is the defending Cincinnati champion. She is seven wins into a streak. She has the best form of any player in the world right now, men's or women's draw.

Is she the US Open favourite?

---

stories.title: Shelton Eliminated in R2 by Faria — Reigning Montreal Champion Out; Eala Advances

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text:
Ben Shelton — reigning Montreal champion, No. 5 seed — is out of Cincinnati.

Lost to Jaime Faria (POR) 6-4, 6-4 in R2.

Meanwhile Eala (PHI) is into R3 after beating Ruse, and faces No. 10 Anisimova tonight.

#CincinnatiOpen #Tennis

facebook.long_form:
Ben Shelton walked into Cincinnati as the reigning Canadian Masters champion — having won back-to-back titles in Montreal last week. He was the No. 5 seed. He was supposed to be the American story of Cincinnati.

Instead, Jaime Faria (POR) sent him home. 6-4, 6-4. No drama, no injury excuse, just a clean loss in the second round.

It's a reminder that tennis doesn't hand out continuation stories. You have to earn every match on every surface, and Saturday, Faria was better.

On the other side of the coin: Alexandra Eala is very much still earning her moments. The Philippine star — who won the DC Open title just two weeks ago — beat Elena-Gabriela Ruse 6-1, 3-0 (retired) in R2 to move into the third round. She now has a 22-9 record on hard courts in 2026. Tonight she faces Amanda Anisimova (USA, approximately No. 10 in the world) in their first career meeting. This is the kind of stage that defines players.

Eala. Cincinnati. Under the lights. Can she keep this run going?

---

facebook.long_form:
Monday is a full R3 day in Cincinnati — and by Tuesday morning, the quarterfinal picture should be clear.

On the WTA side: Elena Rybakina (the defending Cincinnati champion) faces Magdalena Frech at 12:30 PM. She leads the H2H 3-0. Iga Swiatek — on a seven-match win streak after Toronto — takes on Maria Sakkari at 3:00 PM, H2H 5-4 to Swiatek. Aryna Sabalenka plays Wang Xinyu on Tuesday; she's not on today's schedule.

On the ATP side: Thiago Agustín Tirante — who stunned Djokovic in R2 — plays the morning R3 match against Martín Landaluce. Rafael Jodar faces Alejandro Tabilo in the afternoon (Jodar leads their 2026 H2H 1-0 but Tabilo won in Indian Wells 2026). And then the night session features the biggest remaining match: No. 1 seed Alexander Zverev takes on Terence Atmane not before 8:30 PM. With Djokovic already gone, Zverev has to deliver.

Quiet day, big stakes. The QF bracket is about to arrive.

---

stories.title: US Open Countdown — Raducanu OUT With Stress Fracture; Alcaraz Eyes Winston-Salem Return

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text:
US Open 2026 withdrawal list:

Raducanu OUT — stress fracture, right leg
Andreescu OUT — stress fracture, back
Djokovic — no warm-up (Cincinnati R2 loss)
Alcaraz — eyeing Winston-Salem for match practice

Main draw starts Aug 30. Draw ceremony Aug 27.

#USOpen2026 #Tennis

facebook.long_form:
The US Open withdrawal list is growing — and two former champions are already out.

Emma Raducanu, who won the 2021 US Open as a qualifier in one of the most stunning runs in the tournament's history, will not be in New York. A stress fracture in her right lower leg — sustained during the grass-court season — ends her 2026 campaign before the year's final Grand Slam. Bianca Andreescu, who lifted the 2019 trophy, is also out with a stress fracture, this time in her back.

For Carlos Alcaraz, the picture is more hopeful but still uncertain. The defending US Open champion hasn't played a competitive match since April — a four-month absence due to wrist tenosynovitis. His team is reportedly eyeing the Winston-Salem Open (ATP 250, starting August 23) as a way to get competitive match practice before the main draw on August 30. That would mean one week of tennis before defending the biggest title of his career.

Jannik Sinner remains on track. The world No. 1 completed a precautionary knee check-up and sources say the situation has not worsened. He's targeting New York.

US Open Fan Week begins August 23. Draw ceremony August 27. Main draw August 30.

Who do you think wins?

---
